```python
import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.appsi.solvers.highs import Highs

def solve(params):
    foods = ["Chicken", "Tuna", "Eggs", "Beef", "Rice", "Apples", "Bread"]

    protein = params["protein_grams"]
    carbs = params["carb_grams"]
    cal = params["calories"]
    price = params["prices"]

    # Map food names to their position in the lists (lists may be passed by params)
    p_protein = {f: protein[i] for i, f in enumerate(foods)}
    p_carbs = {f: carbs[i] for i, f in enumerate(foods)}
    p_cal = {f: cal[i] for i, f in enumerate(foods)}
    p_price = {f: price[i] for i, f in enumerate(foods)}

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    model.foods = pyo.Set(initialize=foods)

    model.x = pyo.Var(model.foods, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    model.protein = pyo.Constraint(
        expr=sum(p_protein[f] * model.x[f] for f in foods) >= params["protein_target"]
    )
    model.carbs = pyo.Constraint(
        expr=sum(p_carbs[f] * model.x[f] for f in foods) >= params["carb_target"]
    )
    model.calories = pyo.Constraint(
        expr=sum(p_cal[f] * model.x[f] for f in foods) >= params["calorie_target"]
    )

    model.cost = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(p_price[f] * model.x[f] for f in foods), sense=pyo.minimize
    )

    Highs().solve(model)
    obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.cost))
    return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
```

#### B-structured.py

```python
# IR:
# {
#   "sets": {"foods": ["Chicken", "Tuna", "Eggs", "Beef", "Rice", "Apples", "Bread"]},
#   "params": {
#     "protein_grams": "food-indexed protein; mapping or sequence in foods order",
#     "carb_grams": "food-indexed carbohydrates; mapping or sequence in foods order",
#     "calories": "food-indexed calories; mapping or sequence in foods order",
#     "prices": "food-indexed unit costs; mapping or sequence in foods order",
#     "protein_target": "minimum weekly protein",
#     "carb_target": "minimum weekly carbohydrates",
#     "calorie_target": "minimum weekly calories"
#   },
#   "decision_variables": {"quantity[food]": "nonnegative continuous real"},
#   "constraints": [
#     "sum(protein_grams[food] * quantity[food] for food in foods) >= protein_target",
#     "sum(carb_grams[food] * quantity[food] for food in foods) >= carb_target",
#     "sum(calories[food] * quantity[food] for food in foods) >= calorie_target"
#   ],
#   "objective": "minimize sum(prices[food] * quantity[food] for food in foods)"
# }

from collections.abc import Mapping

import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.appsi.solvers.highs import Highs


def solve(params):
    foods = ("Chicken", "Tuna", "Eggs", "Beef", "Rice", "Apples", "Bread")

    def by_food(values):
        if isinstance(values, Mapping):
            return {food: values[food] for food in foods}
        return {food: values[position] for position, food in enumerate(foods)}

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    model.foods = pyo.Set(initialize=foods, ordered=True)

    model.protein_grams = pyo.Param(
        model.foods, initialize=by_food(params["protein_grams"])
    )
    model.carb_grams = pyo.Param(
        model.foods, initialize=by_food(params["carb_grams"])
    )
    model.calories = pyo.Param(
        model.foods, initialize=by_food(params["calories"])
    )
    model.prices = pyo.Param(
        model.foods, initialize=by_food(params["prices"])
    )
    model.protein_target = pyo.Param(initialize=params["protein_target"])
    model.carb_target = pyo.Param(initialize=params["carb_target"])
    model.calorie_target = pyo.Param(initialize=params["calorie_target"])

    model.quantity = pyo.Var(model.foods, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    model.protein_requirement = pyo.Constraint(
        expr=sum(
            model.protein_grams[food] * model.quantity[food]
            for food in model.foods
        ) >= model.protein_target
    )
    model.carb_requirement = pyo.Constraint(
        expr=sum(
            model.carb_grams[food] * model.quantity[food]
            for food in model.foods
        ) >= model.carb_target
    )
    model.calorie_requirement = pyo.Constraint(
        expr=sum(
            model.calories[food] * model.quantity[food]
            for food in model.foods
        ) >= model.calorie_target
    )

    model.total_cost = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(
            model.prices[food] * model.quantity[food]
            for food in model.foods
        ),
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    try:
        Highs().solve(model)
    except RuntimeError:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "solve_failed"}

    try:
        obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.total_cost))
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        return {"objective": None, "status": "objective_unavailable"}

    return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
```

```python
import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.appsi.solvers.highs import Highs


def solve(params):
    cities = ["E", "F", "G", "H", "I"]

    cost = {
        ("E", "F"): params["cost_E_F"],
        ("E", "G"): params["cost_E_G"],
        ("E", "H"): params["cost_E_H"],
        ("E", "I"): params["cost_E_I"],
        ("F", "E"): params["cost_F_E"],
        ("F", "G"): params["cost_F_G"],
        ("F", "H"): params["cost_F_H"],
        ("F", "I"): params["cost_F_I"],
        ("G", "E"): params["cost_G_E"],
        ("G", "F"): params["cost_G_F"],
        ("G", "H"): params["cost_G_H"],
        ("G", "I"): params["cost_G_I"],
        ("H", "E"): params["cost_H_E"],
        ("H", "F"): params["cost_H_F"],
        ("H", "G"): params["cost_H_G"],
        ("H", "I"): params["cost_H_I"],
        ("I", "E"): params["cost_I_E"],
        ("I", "F"): params["cost_I_F"],
        ("I", "G"): params["cost_I_G"],
        ("I", "H"): params["cost_I_H"],
    }

    arcs = [(a, b) for a in cities for b in cities if a != b]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    model.ARC = pyo.Set(initialize=arcs, dimen=2)
    model.CITY = pyo.Set(initialize=cities)

    model.x = pyo.Var(model.ARC, domain=pyo.Binary)
    model.u = pyo.Var(model.CITY, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(cost[(a, b)] * m.x[(a, b)] for (a, b) in m.ARC)

    model.total_cost = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    def out_rule(m, a):
        return sum(m.x[(a, b)] for b in cities if b != a) == 1

    def in_rule(m, b):
        return sum(m.x[(a, b)] for a in cities if a != b) == 1

    model.out_cons = pyo.Constraint(model.CITY, rule=out_rule)
    model.in_cons = pyo.Constraint(model.CITY, rule=in_rule)

    # Subtour elimination (MTZ). Fix u[E] = 0 as the anchor to break symmetry.
    model.u["E"].fix(0)

    def mtz_rule(m, a, b):
        if a != b and a != "E" and b != "E":
            return m.u[a] - m.u[b] + len(cities) * m.x[(a, b)] <= len(cities) - 1
        return pyo.Constraint.Skip

    model.mtz_cons = pyo.Constraint(model.ARC, rule=mtz_rule)

    Highs().solve(model)
    obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.total_cost))
    return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
```

```python
from itertools import combinations

import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.appsi.solvers.highs import Highs


def solve(params):
    cities = ("E", "F", "G", "H", "I")
    arcs = tuple(
        (origin, destination)
        for origin in cities
        for destination in cities
        if origin != destination
    )

    costs = {
        ("E", "F"): params["cost_E_F"],
        ("E", "G"): params["cost_E_G"],
        ("E", "H"): params["cost_E_H"],
        ("E", "I"): params["cost_E_I"],
        ("F", "E"): params["cost_F_E"],
        ("F", "G"): params["cost_F_G"],
        ("F", "H"): params["cost_F_H"],
        ("F", "I"): params["cost_F_I"],
        ("G", "E"): params["cost_G_E"],
        ("G", "F"): params["cost_G_F"],
        ("G", "H"): params["cost_G_H"],
        ("G", "I"): params["cost_G_I"],
        ("H", "E"): params["cost_H_E"],
        ("H", "F"): params["cost_H_F"],
        ("H", "G"): params["cost_H_G"],
        ("H", "I"): params["cost_H_I"],
        ("I", "E"): params["cost_I_E"],
        ("I", "F"): params["cost_I_F"],
        ("I", "G"): params["cost_I_G"],
        ("I", "H"): params["cost_I_H"],
    }

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    model.cities = pyo.Set(initialize=cities, ordered=True)
    model.arcs = pyo.Set(dimen=2, initialize=arcs, ordered=True)
    model.cost = pyo.Param(model.arcs, initialize=costs, within=pyo.Reals)
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.arcs, domain=pyo.Binary)

    def outgoing_rule(model, origin):
        return sum(
            model.x[origin, destination]
            for destination in model.cities
            if destination != origin
        ) == 1

    def incoming_rule(model, destination):
        return sum(
            model.x[origin, destination]
            for origin in model.cities
            if origin != destination
        ) == 1

    model.outgoing = pyo.Constraint(model.cities, rule=outgoing_rule)
    model.incoming = pyo.Constraint(model.cities, rule=incoming_rule)

    model.subtour_limits = pyo.ConstraintList()
    for subset_size in range(2, len(cities)):
        for subset in combinations(cities, subset_size):
            model.subtour_limits.add(
                sum(
                    model.x[origin, destination]
                    for origin in subset
                    for destination in subset
                    if origin != destination
                )
                <= len(subset) - 1
            )

    model.total_cost = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(
            model.cost[origin, destination] * model.x[origin, destination]
            for origin, destination in model.arcs
        ),
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    try:
        Highs().solve(model)
    except RuntimeError:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "solver_failed"}

    try:
        obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.total_cost))
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        return {"objective": None, "status": "no_objective"}

    return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
```

```python
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

def solve(params):
    cities = ['E', 'F', 'G', 'H', 'I']
    n = len(cities)
    idx = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(cities)}

    cost = {}
    for src in cities:
        for dst in cities:
            if src != dst:
                key = f"cost_{src}_{dst}"
                cost[src, dst] = params[key]

    model = gp.Model("TSP")
    model.setParam("OutputFlag", 0)

    x = model.addVars(cities, cities, vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="x")
    u = model.addVars(cities, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="u")

    # No self-loops
    for c in cities:
        model.addConstr(x[c, c] == 0)

    # Each city is left exactly once
    for src in cities:
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[src, dst] for dst in cities if dst != src) == 1)

    # Each city is entered exactly once
    for dst in cities:
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[src, dst] for src in cities if src != dst) == 1)

    # MTZ subtour elimination
    for c in cities:
        model.addConstr(u[c] >= 0)
        model.addConstr(u[c] <= n - 1)

    for src in cities:
        for dst in cities:
            if src != dst and dst != cities[0]:
                model.addConstr(u[src] - u[dst] + n * x[src, dst] <= n - 1)

    model.setObjective(
        gp.quicksum(cost[src, dst] * x[src, dst] for src in cities for dst in cities if src != dst),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    model.optimize()

    if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
        return {"objective": model.ObjVal, "status": "optimal"}
    elif model.Status == GRB.INFEASIBLE:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "infeasible"}
    else:
        return {"objective": None, "status": f"status_{model.Status}"}
```

```python
import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.appsi.solvers.highs import Highs


def solve(params):
    nodes = [1, 2, 3, 4]

    cost = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                cost[(i, j)] = params["c{}{}".format(i, j)]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    model.arcs = pyo.Set(initialize=[(i, j) for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j])
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.arcs, domain=pyo.Binary)

    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(cost[(i, j)] * m.x[(i, j)] for (i, j) in m.arcs)

    model.total_cost = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    def out_rule(m, i):
        return sum(m.x[(i, j)] for j in nodes if j != i) == 1

    def in_rule(m, j):
        return sum(m.x[(i, j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1

    model.out_flow = pyo.Constraint(nodes, rule=out_rule)
    model.in_flow = pyo.Constraint(nodes, rule=in_rule)

    # Subtour elimination (MTZ) for the single tour
    n = len(nodes)
    order = list(range(n + 1))

    def u_bounds(m, i):
        return (1, n - 1)

    model.u = pyo.Var(order[1:], bounds=u_bounds)

    def mtz_rule(m, i, j):
        if i != j and i != 1 and j != 1 and i in order[1:] and j in order[1:]:
            return m.u[i] - m.u[j] + (n - 1) * m.x[(i, j)] <= n - 2
        return pyo.Constraint.Skip

    model.mtz = pyo.Constraint([(i, j) for i in order[1:] for j in order[1:]], rule=mtz_rule)

    solver = Highs()
    solver.solve(model)

    obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.total_cost))
    return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
```

```python
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

def solve(params):
    c12 = params["c12"]
    c13 = params["c13"]
    c14 = params["c14"]
    c21 = params["c21"]
    c23 = params["c23"]
    c24 = params["c24"]
    c31 = params["c31"]
    c32 = params["c32"]
    c34 = params["c34"]
    c41 = params["c41"]
    c42 = params["c42"]
    c43 = params["c43"]

    n = 4
    cities = [1, 2, 3, 4]

    cost = {
        (1, 2): c12, (1, 3): c13, (1, 4): c14,
        (2, 1): c21, (2, 3): c23, (2, 4): c24,
        (3, 1): c31, (3, 2): c32, (3, 4): c34,
        (4, 1): c41, (4, 2): c42, (4, 3): c43,
    }

    arcs = list(cost.keys())

    model = gp.Model("TSP_4cities")
    model.setParam("OutputFlag", 0)

    x = model.addVars(arcs, vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="x")

    # Subtour elimination via MTZ
    u = model.addVars(cities, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="u", lb=1, ub=n)

    # Objective
    model.setObjective(gp.quicksum(cost[i, j] * x[i, j] for (i, j) in arcs), GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # Each city is left exactly once
    for i in cities:
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for j in cities if j != i) == 1, name=f"leave_{i}")

    # Each city is entered exactly once
    for j in cities:
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for i in cities if i != j) == 1, name=f"enter_{j}")

    # MTZ subtour elimination (city 1 is the reference node)
    for i in cities:
        for j in cities:
            if i != j and i != 1 and j != 1:
                model.addConstr(u[i] - u[j] + n * x[i, j] <= n - 1, name=f"mtz_{i}_{j}")

    model.optimize()

    if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
        return {"objective": model.ObjVal, "status": "optimal"}
    elif model.Status == GRB.INFEASIBLE:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "infeasible"}
    else:
        return {"objective": None, "status": f"status_{model.Status}"}
```

#### A-direct.py

```python
import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.appsi.solvers.highs import Highs


def solve(params):
    locations = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]

    # Build cost dictionary from params
    cost = {}
    for i in locations:
        for j in locations:
            if i != j:
                cost[(i, j)] = params["cost_{}_{}".format(i, j)]

    arcs = [(i, j) for i in locations for j in locations if i != j]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.L = pyo.Set(initialize=locations)
    model.A = pyo.Set(initialize=arcs, dimen=2)

    model.cost = pyo.Param(model.A, initialize=cost)

    model.x = pyo.Var(model.A, domain=pyo.Binary)

    # Objective: minimize total travel cost
    def obj_rule(mod):
        return sum(mod.cost[i, j] * mod.x[i, j] for (i, j) in mod.A)

    model.total_cost = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Each location has exactly one outgoing arc
    def out_rule(mod, i):
        return sum(mod.x[i, j] for j in mod.L if j != i) == 1

    model.out_cons = pyo.Constraint(model.L, rule=out_rule)

    # Each location has exactly one incoming arc
    def in_rule(mod, j):
        return sum(mod.x[i, j] for i in mod.L if i != j) == 1

    model.in_cons = pyo.Constraint(model.L, rule=in_rule)

    # Subtour elimination (MTZ) with continuous order variables
    model.u = pyo.Var(model.L, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, len(locations)))
    model.u[1].setlb(1)
    model.u[1].setub(1)

    for i in locations:
        for j in locations:
            if i != 1 and i != j and j != 1:
                model.add_component(
                    "mtz_%d_%d" % (i, j),
                    pyo.Constraint(
                        expr=model.u[i] - model.u[j] + len(locations) * model.x[i, j]
                        <= len(locations) - 1
                    ),
                )

    solver = Highs()
    solver.solve(model)

    obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.total_cost))
    return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
```

```python
# IR: {"sets":{"V":[1,2,3,4,5,6],"A":"{(i,j) in V x V: i != j}","S":"{S subset V: 2 <= |S| <= 5}"},"params":{"cost[i,j]":"params[f'cost_{i}_{j}'] for (i,j) in A, real"},"variables":{"x[i,j]":"binary for (i,j) in A"},"constraints":["sum(x[i,j] for j in V if j != i) = 1 for each i in V","sum(x[i,j] for i in V if i != j) = 1 for each j in V","sum(x[i,j] for i in S for j in S if i != j) <= |S|-1 for each S in S"],"objective":"minimize sum(cost[i,j]*x[i,j] for (i,j) in A)"}

from itertools import combinations

import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.appsi.solvers.highs import Highs


def solve(params):
    locations = tuple(range(1, 7))
    arcs = tuple(
        (origin, destination)
        for origin in locations
        for destination in locations
        if origin != destination
    )
    costs = {
        (origin, destination): params[f"cost_{origin}_{destination}"]
        for origin, destination in arcs
    }

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    model.locations = pyo.Set(initialize=locations, ordered=True)
    model.arcs = pyo.Set(dimen=2, initialize=arcs, ordered=True)
    model.travel_cost = pyo.Param(
        model.arcs,
        initialize=costs,
        within=pyo.Reals,
    )
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.arcs, domain=pyo.Binary)

    def outgoing_rule(instance, origin):
        return sum(
            instance.x[origin, destination]
            for destination in instance.locations
            if destination != origin
        ) == 1

    def incoming_rule(instance, destination):
        return sum(
            instance.x[origin, destination]
            for origin in instance.locations
            if origin != destination
        ) == 1

    model.outgoing = pyo.Constraint(model.locations, rule=outgoing_rule)
    model.incoming = pyo.Constraint(model.locations, rule=incoming_rule)

    model.subtour_elimination = pyo.ConstraintList()
    for subset_size in range(2, len(locations)):
        for subset in combinations(locations, subset_size):
            model.subtour_elimination.add(
                sum(
                    model.x[origin, destination]
                    for origin in subset
                    for destination in subset
                    if origin != destination
                )
                <= subset_size - 1
            )

    model.total_cost = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(
            model.travel_cost[origin, destination]
            * model.x[origin, destination]
            for origin, destination in model.arcs
        ),
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    try:
        Highs().solve(model)
    except RuntimeError:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "solver_failed"}

    try:
        obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.total_cost))
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        return {"objective": None, "status": "objective_unavailable"}

    return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
```

```python
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB
from itertools import combinations

def solve(params):
    n = 6
    nodes = list(range(1, n + 1))

    # Build cost dict from params
    cost = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                cost[i, j] = params[f"cost_{i}_{j}"]

    model = gp.Model("TSP")
    model.setParam("OutputFlag", 0)

    # Binary decision variables x[i,j] = 1 if travel from i to j
    x = model.addVars(
        [(i, j) for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j],
        vtype=GRB.BINARY,
        name="x"
    )

    # MTZ subtour elimination variables
    u = model.addVars(nodes, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="u")

    # Objective: minimize total travel cost
    model.setObjective(
        gp.quicksum(cost[i, j] * x[i, j] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # Each node is left exactly once
    for i in nodes:
        model.addConstr(
            gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for j in nodes if j != i) == 1,
            name=f"leave_{i}"
        )

    # Each node is entered exactly once
    for j in nodes:
        model.addConstr(
            gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1,
            name=f"enter_{j}"
        )

    # MTZ subtour elimination constraints
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j and j != 1:
                model.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + n * x[i, j] <= n - 1,
                    name=f"mtz_{i}_{j}"
                )

    model.optimize()

    if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
        return {"objective": model.ObjVal, "status": "optimal"}
    elif model.Status == GRB.INFEASIBLE:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "infeasible"}
    elif model.Status == GRB.UNBOUNDED:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "unbounded"}
    else:
        return {"objective": None, "status": f"status_{model.Status}"}
```

```python
import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.appsi.solvers.highs import Highs


def solve(params):
    cities = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
    n = len(cities)
    arcs = [(i, j) for i in cities for j in cities if i != j]

    cost = {}
    for i in cities:
        for j in cities:
            if i != j:
                cost[(i, j)] = params[f"cost_{i}_{j}"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.arcs = pyo.Set(initialize=arcs, dimen=2)
    model.cities = pyo.Set(initialize=cities)

    model.x = pyo.Var(model.arcs, domain=pyo.Binary)
    model.u = pyo.Var(model.cities, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(cost[(i, j)] * m.x[(i, j)] for (i, j) in arcs)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    def out_rule(m, i):
        return sum(m.x[(i, j)] for j in cities if j != i) == 1

    def in_rule(m, j):
        return sum(m.x[(i, j)] for i in cities if i != j) == 1

    model.out_cons = pyo.Constraint(model.cities, rule=out_rule)
    model.in_cons = pyo.Constraint(model.cities, rule=in_rule)

    model.u[1].fix(1)

    def mtz_rule(m, i, j):
        if i != 1 and j != 1 and i != j:
            return m.u[i] - m.u[j] + (n - 1) * m.x[(i, j)] <= n - 2
        return pyo.Constraint.Skip

    model.mtz = pyo.Constraint(model.arcs, rule=mtz_rule)

    def u_bound_rule(m, i):
        return m.u[i] <= n

    model.u_bound = pyo.Constraint(model.cities, rule=u_bound_rule)

    Highs().solve(model)

    obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.obj))
    return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
```

```python
import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.appsi.solvers.highs import Highs


def solve(params):
    cities = (1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
    arcs = [(i, j) for i in cities for j in cities if i != j]

    costs = {
        (1, 2): params["cost_1_2"],
        (1, 3): params["cost_1_3"],
        (1, 4): params["cost_1_4"],
        (1, 5): params["cost_1_5"],
        (2, 1): params["cost_2_1"],
        (2, 3): params["cost_2_3"],
        (2, 4): params["cost_2_4"],
        (2, 5): params["cost_2_5"],
        (3, 1): params["cost_3_1"],
        (3, 2): params["cost_3_2"],
        (3, 4): params["cost_3_4"],
        (3, 5): params["cost_3_5"],
        (4, 1): params["cost_4_1"],
        (4, 2): params["cost_4_2"],
        (4, 3): params["cost_4_3"],
        (4, 5): params["cost_4_5"],
        (5, 1): params["cost_5_1"],
        (5, 2): params["cost_5_2"],
        (5, 3): params["cost_5_3"],
        (5, 4): params["cost_5_4"],
    }

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    model.cities = pyo.Set(initialize=cities, ordered=True)
    model.arcs = pyo.Set(dimen=2, initialize=arcs, ordered=True)
    model.cost = pyo.Param(
        model.arcs, initialize=costs, within=pyo.Reals
    )
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.arcs, domain=pyo.Binary)

    def outgoing_rule(instance, i):
        return sum(
            instance.x[i, j] for j in instance.cities if j != i
        ) == 1

    def incoming_rule(instance, j):
        return sum(
            instance.x[i, j] for i in instance.cities if i != j
        ) == 1

    model.outgoing = pyo.Constraint(model.cities, rule=outgoing_rule)
    model.incoming = pyo.Constraint(model.cities, rule=incoming_rule)

    model.subtour_elimination = pyo.ConstraintList()
    for subset_size in range(2, len(cities)):
        for subset in combinations(cities, subset_size):
            model.subtour_elimination.add(
                sum(
                    model.x[i, j]
                    for i in subset
                    for j in subset
                    if i != j
                )
                <= len(subset) - 1
            )

    model.total_cost = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(
            model.cost[i, j] * model.x[i, j] for i, j in model.arcs
        ),
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    try:
        Highs().solve(model)
    except RuntimeError:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "infeasible_or_failed"}

    try:
        obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.total_cost))
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        return {"objective": None, "status": "objective_unavailable"}

    return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
```

```python
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB
from itertools import combinations

def solve(params):
    n = 5
    cities = list(range(1, n + 1))

    # Build cost dict from params
    cost = {}
    for i in cities:
        for j in cities:
            if i != j:
                cost[i, j] = params[f"cost_{i}_{j}"]

    model = gp.Model("TSP")
    model.setParam("OutputFlag", 0)

    # Binary decision variables x[i,j] = 1 if travel from i to j
    x = model.addVars(cities, cities, vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="x")

    # No self-loops
    for i in cities:
        model.addConstr(x[i, i] == 0)

    # Objective: minimize total travel cost
    model.setObjective(
        gp.quicksum(cost[i, j] * x[i, j] for i in cities for j in cities if i != j),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # Each city must be left exactly once
    for i in cities:
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for j in cities if j != i) == 1)

    # Each city must be entered exactly once
    for j in cities:
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for i in cities if i != j) == 1)

    # MTZ subtour elimination
    u = model.addVars(cities, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="u")
    for i in cities:
        u[i].lb = 1
        u[i].ub = n

    # Fix u[1] = 1 (arbitrary starting city for MTZ)
    model.addConstr(u[1] == 1)

    for i in cities:
        for j in cities:
            if i != j and j != 1:
                model.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + n * x[i, j] <= n - 1
                )

    model.optimize()

    if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
        return {"objective": model.ObjVal, "status": "optimal"}
    elif model.Status == GRB.INFEASIBLE:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "infeasible"}
    elif model.Status == GRB.UNBOUNDED:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "unbounded"}
    else:
        return {"objective": None, "status": f"status_{model.Status}"}
```

```
In a scenario involving a salesperson who needs to visit five different cities to conduct business, each city is uniquely numbered from 1 to 5. The salesperson's objective is to minimize the total travel expenses, which could be influenced by factors such as distance, fuel costs, or transportation fees. The salesperson can start their journey from any of these cities but must ensure they visit each city exactly once before returning to their starting point.

The travel costs between the cities are as follows:
- From City 1, the travel costs are 58 units to City 2, 15 units to City 3, 75 units to City 4, and 91 units to City 5.
- From City 2, it costs 58 units to City 1, 54 units to City 3, 85 units to City 4, and 11 units to City 5.
- Traveling from City 3, the expenses are 15 units to City 1, 54 units to City 2, 28 units to City 4, and 61 units to City 5.
- From City 4, the costs are 75 units to City 1, 85 units to City 2, 28 units to City 3, and 47 units to City 5.
- Lastly, from City 5, it costs 91 units to City 1, 11 units to City 2, 61 units to City 3, and 47 units to City 4.

Given this setup, what is the minimum total travel cost for the salesperson to visit each city exactly once and then return to the starting city?
```

```python
import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.appsi.solvers.highs import Highs


def solve(params):
    cost = params["cost_matrix"]
    cities = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.i = pyo.Set(initialize=cities)
    model.j = pyo.Set(initialize=cities)

    # x[i,j] = 1 if edge i->j is used (i != j)
    model.x = pyo.Var(
        [(l, k) for l in cities for k in cities if l != k],
        domain=pyo.Binary,
    )

    # u[k] = position/order of city k along the tour (MTZ subtour elimination)
    model.u = pyo.Var(cities, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(1, 5))

    def obj_rule(mod):
        return sum(
            cost[l - 1][k - 1] * mod.x[l, k]
            for l in cities for k in cities if l != k
        )

    model.total_cost = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Each city has exactly one outgoing edge
    def out_rule(mod, l):
        return sum(mod.x[l, k] for k in cities if k != l) == 1

    model.out_cons = pyo.Constraint(cities, rule=out_rule)

    # Each city has exactly one incoming edge
    def in_rule(mod, k):
        return sum(mod.x[l, k] for l in cities if l != k) == 1

    model.in_cons = pyo.Constraint(cities, rule=in_rule)

    # MTZ subtour elimination: u[i] - u[j] + n*x[i,j] <= n-1 for i,j != depot
    n = len(cities)
    non_depot = [1, 2, 3, 4]  # city 5 treated as depot

    def mtz_rule(mod, l, k):
        return mod.u[l] - mod.u[k] + n * mod.x[l, k] <= n - 1

    model.mtz = pyo.Constraint(
        [(l, k) for l in non_depot for k in non_depot if l != k],
        rule=mtz_rule,
    )

    # Fix depot ordering bound
    model.depot_order = pyo.Constraint(expr=model.u[5] == 1)
    model.u1_lb = pyo.Constraint(expr=model.u[1] >= 2)

    solver = Highs()
    solver.solve(model)

    obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.total_cost))
    return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
```

```python
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB
from itertools import combinations

def solve(params):
    cost_matrix = params["cost_matrix"]
    n = 5
    cities = list(range(1, n + 1))

    model = gp.Model("TSP")
    model.setParam("OutputFlag", 0)

    # Decision variables: x[i,j] = 1 if travel from city i to city j
    x = {}
    for i in cities:
        for j in cities:
            if i != j:
                x[i, j] = model.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"x_{i}_{j}")

    # Objective: minimize total travel cost
    model.setObjective(
        gp.quicksum(cost_matrix[i - 1][j - 1] * x[i, j] for i in cities for j in cities if i != j),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # Each city must be left exactly once
    for i in cities:
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for j in cities if j != i) == 1, name=f"leave_{i}")

    # Each city must be entered exactly once
    for j in cities:
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for i in cities if i != j) == 1, name=f"enter_{j}")

    # Subtour elimination using MTZ formulation
    u = {}
    for i in cities:
        u[i] = model.addVar(lb=1, ub=n, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"u_{i}")

    for i in cities:
        for j in cities:
            if i != j and j != 1:
                model.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + n * x[i, j] <= n - 1,
                    name=f"mtz_{i}_{j}"
                )

    model.optimize()

    if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
        return {"objective": model.ObjVal, "status": "optimal"}
    elif model.Status == GRB.INFEASIBLE:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "infeasible"}
    else:
        return {"objective": None, "status": f"status_{model.Status}"}
```

```python
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    # Each city: exactly one outgoing arc
    model.out_cons = pyo.Constraint(
        cities,
        rule=lambda m, i: sum(m.x[i, j] for j in cities if (i, j) in cost) == 1,
    )
    # Each city: exactly one incoming arc
    model.in_cons = pyo.Constraint(
        cities,
        rule=lambda m, j: sum(m.x[i, j] for i in cities if (i, j) in cost) == 1,
    )

    # Subtour elimination (MTZ). With 4 nodes, prevent 2-cycles directly.
    # A 2-cycle is x[i,j]+x[j,i] <= 1.
    pairs = [(1, 2), (1, 3), (1, 4), (2, 3), (2, 4), (3, 4)]
    model.arc_2cycle = pyo.Constraint(
        pairs,
        rule=lambda m, i, j: m.x[i, j] + m.x[j, i] <= 1,
    )

    Highs().solve(model)
    obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.obj))
    return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
```

```python
from itertools import combinations

import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.appsi.solvers.highs import Highs


def solve(params):
    cities = (1, 2, 3, 4)
    arcs = [(i, j) for i in cities for j in cities if i != j]
    subsets = [
        subset
        for size in range(2, len(cities))
        for subset in combinations(cities, size)
    ]

    costs = {
        (1, 2): params["travel_cost_c1_c2"],
        (1, 3): params["travel_cost_c1_c3"],
        (1, 4): params["travel_cost_c1_c4"],
        (2, 1): params["travel_cost_c2_c1"],
        (2, 3): params["travel_cost_c2_c3"],
        (2, 4): params["travel_cost_c2_c4"],
        (3, 1): params["travel_cost_c3_c1"],
        (3, 2): params["travel_cost_c3_c2"],
        (3, 4): params["travel_cost_c3_c4"],
        (4, 1): params["travel_cost_c4_c1"],
        (4, 2): params["travel_cost_c4_c2"],
        (4, 3): params["travel_cost_c4_c3"],
    }

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    model.cities = pyo.Set(initialize=cities, ordered=True)
    model.arcs = pyo.Set(dimen=2, initialize=arcs, ordered=True)
    model.cost = pyo.Param(model.arcs, initialize=costs, within=pyo.Reals)
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.arcs, domain=pyo.Binary)

    def outgoing_rule(instance, i):
        return sum(
            instance.x[i, j] for j in instance.cities if j != i
        ) == 1

    def incoming_rule(instance, j):
        return sum(
            instance.x[i, j] for i in instance.cities if i != j
        ) == 1

    model.outgoing = pyo.Constraint(model.cities, rule=outgoing_rule)
    model.incoming = pyo.Constraint(model.cities, rule=incoming_rule)

    model.subtour = pyo.ConstraintList()
    for subset in subsets:
        model.subtour.add(
            sum(
                model.x[i, j]
                for i in subset
                for j in subset
                if i != j
            ) <= len(subset) - 1
        )

    model.total_cost = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(model.cost[i, j] * model.x[i, j] for i, j in model.arcs),
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    try:
        Highs().solve(model)
    except RuntimeError:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "solve_failed"}

    try:
        obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.total_cost))
    except ValueError:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "objective_unavailable"}

    return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
```

```python
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

def solve(params):
    # Build cost matrix from params
    n = 4
    cities = [1, 2, 3, 4]
    
    cost = {}
    cost[(1,2)] = params["travel_cost_c1_c2"]
    cost[(1,3)] = params["travel_cost_c1_c3"]
    cost[(1,4)] = params["travel_cost_c1_c4"]
    cost[(2,1)] = params["travel_cost_c2_c1"]
    cost[(2,3)] = params["travel_cost_c2_c3"]
    cost[(2,4)] = params["travel_cost_c2_c4"]
    cost[(3,1)] = params["travel_cost_c3_c1"]
    cost[(3,2)] = params["travel_cost_c3_c2"]
    cost[(3,4)] = params["travel_cost_c3_c4"]
    cost[(4,1)] = params["travel_cost_c4_c1"]
    cost[(4,2)] = params["travel_cost_c4_c2"]
    cost[(4,3)] = params["travel_cost_c4_c3"]

    arcs = [(i, j) for i in cities for j in cities if i != j]

    model = gp.Model("TSP_4cities")
    model.setParam("OutputFlag", 0)

    # Binary decision variables: x[i,j] = 1 if arc (i->j) is used
    x = model.addVars(arcs, vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="x")

    # Auxiliary variables for MTZ subtour elimination: u[i] position in tour
    u = model.addVars(cities, lb=0.0, ub=n - 1, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="u")

    # Objective: minimize total travel cost
    model.setObjective(gp.quicksum(cost[i, j] * x[i, j] for (i, j) in arcs), GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # Each city must be left exactly once
    for i in cities:
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for j in cities if j != i) == 1, name=f"leave_{i}")

    # Each city must be entered exactly once
    for j in cities:
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for i in cities if i != j) == 1, name=f"enter_{j}")

    # MTZ subtour elimination constraints
    # Fix position of city 1 to break symmetry
    model.addConstr(u[1] == 0, name="u1_fix")
    for i in cities:
        for j in cities:
            if i != j and j != 1:
                model.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + n * x[i, j] <= n - 1,
                    name=f"mtz_{i}_{j}"
                )

    model.optimize()

    if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
        return {"objective": model.ObjVal, "status": "optimal"}
    elif model.Status == GRB.INFEASIBLE:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "infeasible"}
    elif model.Status == GRB.UNBOUNDED:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "unbounded"}
    else:
        return {"objective": None, "status": f"status_{model.Status}"}
```

### 2. Problem text

```
Imagine a scenario where a salesperson must visit four distinct cities to conduct business meetings. Let's label these cities as City 1, City 2, City 3, and City 4. The salesperson can start their trip from any city, but they must visit each city exactly once and then return to the starting point. The main objective is to minimize the total cost of traveling between these cities.

Here’s a detailed breakdown of the travel costs:
- From City 1, the travel cost is 27 units to City 2, 48 units to City 3, and 76 units to City 4.
- From City 2, it costs 27 units to return to City 1, 82 units to reach City 3, and 88 units to go to City 4.
- From City 3, traveling back to City 1 costs 48 units, moving to City 2 costs 82 units, and it is 97 units to journey to City 4.
- Lastly, from City 4, it costs 76 units to go back to City 1, 88 units to travel to City 2, and 97 units to move to City 3.

What is the minimum total travel cost for the salesperson to visit each of these cities exactly once and return to the starting city?
```

```python
import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.appsi.solvers.highs import Highs


def solve(params):
    cities = [1, 2, 3, 4]
    arcs = [(i, j) for i in cities for j in cities if i != j]

    cost_data = {
        (1, 2): params["c12"],
        (1, 3): params["c13"],
        (1, 4): params["c14"],
        (2, 1): params["c21"],
        (2, 3): params["c23"],
        (2, 4): params["c24"],
        (3, 1): params["c31"],
        (3, 2): params["c32"],
        (3, 4): params["c34"],
        (4, 1): params["c41"],
        (4, 2): params["c42"],
        (4, 3): params["c43"],
    }

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.cities = pyo.Set(initialize=cities)
    model.arcs = pyo.Set(initialize=arcs, dimen=2)

    model.x = pyo.Var(model.arcs, domain=pyo.Binary)

    # Each city entered exactly once
    model.in_flow = pyo.Constraint(
        model.cities,
        rule=lambda mm, j: sum(mm.x[i, j] for i in cities if i != j) == 1,
    )

    # Each city left exactly once
    model.out_flow = pyo.Constraint(
        model.cities,
        rule=lambda mm, i: sum(mm.x[i, j] for j in cities if j != i) == 1,
    )

    # Subtour elimination via MTZ for nodes {2,3,4} (anchor node 1)
    order_cities = [2, 3, 4]
    model.u = pyo.Var(order_cities, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    def mtz_rule(mm, i, j):
        if i == 1 or j == 1:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        return mm.u[i] - mm.u[j] + 3 * mm.x[i, j] <= 2

    model.mtz = pyo.Constraint(
        [(i, j) for i in order_cities for j in order_cities if i != j],
        rule=mtz_rule,
    )

    model.u_bounds = pyo.Constraint(
        order_cities,
        rule=lambda mm, i: pyo.inequality(1, mm.u[i], 3),
    )

    def obj_rule(mm):
        return sum(cost_data[i, j] * mm.x[i, j] for (i, j) in arcs)

    model.total_cost = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    Highs().solve(model)

    obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.total_cost))
    return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
```

```python
        model.cities,

        ) == 1,

    model.subtour_elimination = pyo.ConstraintList()

                model.x[i, j]
                for i in subset
                for j in subset

        expr=sum(
            model.travel_cost[i, j] * model.x[i, j]
            for i, j in model.arcs
        ),
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    try:
        Highs().solve(model)
    except RuntimeError:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "solver_failed"}

    try:
        obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.total_cost))
    except ValueError:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "objective_unavailable"}

    return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
```

```
Imagine a salesperson embarking on a journey to visit five distinct cities—let's name them A, B, C, D, and E—to promote their products. The primary objective is to minimize the overall travel cost incurred during this excursion, which encompasses factors such as distance, time, or expenses.

Here's a comprehensive breakdown of the travel costs between the cities:
- Traveling from City A incurs a cost of 44 units to reach B, 19 units to reach C, 92 units to reach D, and 71 units to reach E.
- City B entails a cost of 44 units to travel to A, 22 units to C, 84 units to D, and 63 units to E.
- For City C, the costs are 19 units to A, 22 units to B, 47 units to D, and 89 units to E.
- Moving on to City D, it involves a cost of 92 units to reach A, 84 units to B, 47 units to C, and 78 units to E.
- Finally, from City E, the costs are 71 units to A, 63 units to B, 89 units to C, and 78 units to D.

Given these details, the pivotal question arises: What is the minimum total travel cost for the salesperson to visit each city exactly once and return to the starting city?
```

```python
import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.appsi.solvers.highs import Highs


def solve(params):
    cost = params["cost"]
    n = len(cost)

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # x[i,j] = 1 if the tour goes from city i to city j
    model.x = pyo.Var(range(n), range(n), domain=pyo.Binary)

    # Objective: minimize total travel cost
    model.objective_expr = pyo.Expression(
        expr=sum(cost[i][j] * model.x[i, j]
                 for i in range(n)
                 for j in range(n)
                 if i != j)
    )
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.objective_expr, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Each city is departed from exactly once
    model.out_deg = pyo.ConstraintList()
    for i in range(n):
        model.out_deg.add(
            sum(model.x[i, j] for j in range(n) if j != i) == 1
        )

    # Each city is arrived at exactly once
    model.in_deg = pyo.ConstraintList()
    for j in range(n):
        model.in_deg.add(
            sum(model.x[i, j] for i in range(n) if i != j) == 1
        )

    # Subtour elimination (Miller-Tucker-Zemlin)
    model.u = pyo.Var(range(n), bounds=(1, n - 1))
    model.subtour = pyo.ConstraintList()
    for i in range(1, n):
        for j in range(1, n):
            if i != j:
                model.subtour.add(
                    model.u[i] - model.u[j] + n * model.x[i, j] <= n - 1
                )

    try:
        Highs().solve(model)
        obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.obj))
        return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
    except Exception:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "infeasible"}
```

```python
# IR: {"sets":{"V":[0,1,2,3,4],"A":"{(i,j) in V x V: i != j}","S":"{U subset V: 2 <= |U| <= 4}"},"params":{"cost":"params['cost'][i][j], for (i,j) in A"},"variables":{"x[i,j]":"binary, for (i,j) in A"},"constraints":["For each i in V: sum(x[i,j] for j != i) = 1","For each j in V: sum(x[i,j] for i != j) = 1","For each U in S: sum(x[i,j] for i,j in U with i != j) <= |U| - 1"],"objective":"minimize sum(cost[i,j] * x[i,j] for (i,j) in A)"}

from itertools import combinations

import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.appsi.solvers.highs import Highs


def solve(params):
    cost = params["cost"]
    cities = tuple(range(5))
    arcs = tuple(
        (origin, destination)
        for origin in cities
        for destination in cities
        if origin != destination
    )
    subsets = tuple(
        subset
        for subset_size in range(2, len(cities))
        for subset in combinations(cities, subset_size)
    )

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    model.cities = pyo.Set(initialize=cities, ordered=True)
    model.arcs = pyo.Set(dimen=2, initialize=arcs, ordered=True)
    model.travel_cost = pyo.Param(
        model.arcs,
        initialize=lambda _, origin, destination: cost[origin][destination],
        within=pyo.Reals,
    )
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.arcs, domain=pyo.Binary)

    def departure_rule(instance, origin):
        return sum(
            instance.x[origin, destination]
            for destination in instance.cities
            if destination != origin
        ) == 1

    def arrival_rule(instance, destination):
        return sum(
            instance.x[origin, destination]
            for origin in instance.cities
            if origin != destination
        ) == 1

    model.departure_constraints = pyo.Constraint(
        model.cities, rule=departure_rule
    )
    model.arrival_constraints = pyo.Constraint(
        model.cities, rule=arrival_rule
    )
    model.subtour_constraints = pyo.ConstraintList()
    for subset in subsets:
        model.subtour_constraints.add(
            sum(
                model.x[origin, destination]
                for origin in subset
                for destination in subset
                if origin != destination
            ) <= len(subset) - 1
        )

    model.total_cost = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(
            model.travel_cost[origin, destination]
            * model.x[origin, destination]
            for origin, destination in model.arcs
        ),
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    try:
        Highs().solve(model)
    except RuntimeError:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "solver_failed"}

    try:
        obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.total_cost))
    except ValueError:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "objective_unavailable"}

    return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
```

```python
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

def solve(params):
    cost = params["cost"]
    n = len(cost)
    cities = range(n)

    model = gp.Model("tsp")
    model.Params.OutputFlag = 0

    x = model.addVars(cities, cities, vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="x")

    model.setObjective(
        gp.quicksum(cost[i][j] * x[i, j] for i in cities for j in cities if i != j),
        GRB.MINIMIZE,
    )

    for i in cities:
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for j in cities if j != i) == 1)
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[j, i] for j in cities if j != i) == 1)
    for i in cities:
        model.addConstr(x[i, i] == 0)

    # Subtour elimination (lazy via callbacks is overkill for n=5; add full formulation)
    from itertools import combinations
    for r in range(2, n):
        for S in combinations(cities, r):
            model.addConstr(
                gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for i in S for j in S if i != j) <= len(S) - 1
            )

    model.optimize()

    if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
        return {"objective": model.ObjVal, "status": "optimal"}
    return {"objective": None, "status": "infeasible"}
```

```python
import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.appsi.solvers.highs import Highs


def solve(params):
    cities = [1, 2, 3, 4]
    arcs = [(i, j) for i in cities for j in cities if i != j]

    def travel_cost(i, j):
        return params["cost_{}_{}".format(i, j)]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.x = pyo.Var(arcs, domain=pyo.Binary)

    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(travel_cost(i, j) * m.x[i, j] for (i, j) in arcs)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Each city entered exactly once
    model.in_deg = pyo.Constraint(
        cities, rule=lambda m, j: sum(m.x[i, j] for i in cities if i != j) == 1
    )

    # Each city left exactly once
    model.out_deg = pyo.Constraint(
        cities, rule=lambda m, i: sum(m.x[i, j] for j in cities if j != i) == 1
    )

    # Subtour elimination (MTZ) for the 4 nodes
    model.u = pyo.Var(cities, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, 4))

    def mtz_rule(m, i, j):
        if i != j and i != 1 and j != 1:
            return m.u[i] - m.u[j] + 4 * m.x[i, j] <= 3
        return pyo.Constraint.Skip

    model.mtz = pyo.Constraint(arcs, rule=mtz_rule)

    Highs().solve(model)

    obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.obj))
    return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
```

```python
        (2, 4): params["cost_2_4"],
        (3, 1): params["cost_3_1"],
        (3, 2): params["cost_3_2"],
        (3, 4): params["cost_3_4"],
        (4, 1): params["cost_4_1"],
        (4, 2): params["cost_4_2"],
        (4, 3): params["cost_4_3"],
    }

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    model.cities = pyo.Set(initialize=cities, ordered=True)
    model.arcs = pyo.Set(dimen=2, initialize=arcs, ordered=True)
    model.travel_cost = pyo.Param(

    )
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.arcs, domain=pyo.Binary)

        return sum(mod.x[i, j] for j in cities if j != i) == 1

    def incoming_rule(mod, j):
        return sum(mod.x[i, j] for i in cities if i != j) == 1

    model.outgoing = pyo.Constraint(model.cities, rule=outgoing_rule)
    model.incoming = pyo.Constraint(model.cities, rule=incoming_rule)

    model.subtour_limits = pyo.ConstraintList()
    for subset in subsets:

            sum(
                model.x[i, j]
                for i in subset
                for j in subset
                if i != j
            )
            <= len(subset) - 1
        )

    model.total_cost = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(
            model.travel_cost[i, j] * model.x[i, j] for i, j in arcs
        ),
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    try:
        Highs().solve(model)

        return {"objective": None, "status": "infeasible_or_failed"}

        obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.total_cost))
```

```python
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

def solve(params):
    n = 4
    cities = list(range(1, n + 1))

    cost = {}
    for i in cities:
        for j in cities:
            if i != j:
                key = f"cost_{i}_{j}"
                cost[(i, j)] = params[key]

    model = gp.Model("TSP")
    model.setParam("OutputFlag", 0)

    # Binary variables: x[i,j] = 1 if travel from city i to city j
    x = {}
    for i in cities:
        for j in cities:
            if i != j:
                x[(i, j)] = model.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"x_{i}_{j}")

    # MTZ subtour elimination variables
    u = {}
    for i in cities:
        u[i] = model.addVar(lb=1, ub=n, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"u_{i}")

    # Objective: minimize total travel cost
    model.setObjective(
        gp.quicksum(cost[(i, j)] * x[(i, j)] for i in cities for j in cities if i != j),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # Each city is departed exactly once
    for i in cities:
        model.addConstr(
            gp.quicksum(x[(i, j)] for j in cities if j != i) == 1,
            name=f"depart_{i}"
        )

    # Each city is arrived at exactly once
    for j in cities:
        model.addConstr(
            gp.quicksum(x[(i, j)] for i in cities if i != j) == 1,
            name=f"arrive_{j}"
        )

    # MTZ subtour elimination constraints
    # Fix u[1] = 1 to break symmetry
    model.addConstr(u[1] == 1, name="u1_fix")
    for i in cities:
        for j in cities:
            if i != j and j != 1:
                model.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + n * x[(i, j)] <= n - 1,
                    name=f"mtz_{i}_{j}"
                )

    model.optimize()

    if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
        return {"objective": model.ObjVal, "status": "optimal"}
    elif model.Status == GRB.INFEASIBLE:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "infeasible"}
    elif model.Status == GRB.UNBOUNDED:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "unbounded"}
    else:
        return {"objective": None, "status": f"status_{model.Status}"}
```

```python
import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.appsi.solvers.highs import Highs


def solve(params):
    cities = ["Alpha", "Bravo", "Charlie", "Delta"]

    cost_dict = {
        ("Alpha", "Bravo"): params["cost_Alpha_Bravo"],
        ("Alpha", "Charlie"): params["cost_Alpha_Charlie"],
        ("Alpha", "Delta"): params["cost_Alpha_Delta"],
        ("Bravo", "Alpha"): params["cost_Bravo_Alpha"],
        ("Bravo", "Charlie"): params["cost_Bravo_Charlie"],
        ("Bravo", "Delta"): params["cost_Bravo_Delta"],
        ("Charlie", "Alpha"): params["cost_Charlie_Alpha"],
        ("Charlie", "Bravo"): params["cost_Charlie_Bravo"],
        ("Charlie", "Delta"): params["cost_Charlie_Delta"],
        ("Delta", "Alpha"): params["cost_Delta_Alpha"],
        ("Delta", "Bravo"): params["cost_Delta_Bravo"],
        ("Delta", "Charlie"): params["cost_Delta_Charlie"],
    }

    arcs = list(cost_dict.keys())

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    model.arcs = pyo.Set(initialize=arcs, dimen=2)
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.arcs, domain=pyo.Binary)

    def objective_rule(mdl):
        return sum(cost_dict[a] * mdl.x[a] for a in arcs)

    model.total_cost = pyo.Objective(rule=objective_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    def out_degree_rule(mdl, c):
        return sum(mdl.x[(c, d)] for d in cities if d != c) == 1

    model.out_degree = pyo.Constraint(cities, rule=out_degree_rule)

    def in_degree_rule(mdl, c):
        return sum(mdl.x[(d, c)] for d in cities if d != c) == 1

    model.in_degree = pyo.Constraint(cities, rule=in_degree_rule)

    subsets = [["Alpha", "Bravo"], ["Alpha", "Charlie"], ["Alpha", "Delta"],
               ["Bravo", "Charlie"], ["Bravo", "Delta"], ["Charlie", "Delta"]]

    def subtour_rule(mdl, k):
        subset = subsets[k]
        internal = [(i, j) for i in subset for j in subset
                    if i != j and (i, j) in cost_dict]
        return sum(mdl.x[a] for a in internal) <= len(subset) - 1

    model.subtour = pyo.Constraint(range(len(subsets)), rule=subtour_rule)

    Highs().solve(model)
    obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.total_cost))
    return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
```

```python
from itertools import combinations

import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.appsi.solvers.highs import Highs


def solve(params):
    cities = ("Alpha", "Bravo", "Charlie", "Delta")
    arcs = [
        (origin, destination)
        for origin in cities
        for destination in cities
        if origin != destination
    ]

    costs = {
        ("Alpha", "Bravo"): params["cost_Alpha_Bravo"],
        ("Alpha", "Charlie"): params["cost_Alpha_Charlie"],
        ("Alpha", "Delta"): params["cost_Alpha_Delta"],
        ("Bravo", "Alpha"): params["cost_Bravo_Alpha"],
        ("Bravo", "Charlie"): params["cost_Bravo_Charlie"],
        ("Bravo", "Delta"): params["cost_Bravo_Delta"],
        ("Charlie", "Alpha"): params["cost_Charlie_Alpha"],
        ("Charlie", "Bravo"): params["cost_Charlie_Bravo"],
        ("Charlie", "Delta"): params["cost_Charlie_Delta"],
        ("Delta", "Alpha"): params["cost_Delta_Alpha"],
        ("Delta", "Bravo"): params["cost_Delta_Bravo"],
        ("Delta", "Charlie"): params["cost_Delta_Charlie"],
    }

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    model.cities = pyo.Set(initialize=cities, ordered=True)
    model.arcs = pyo.Set(dimen=2, initialize=arcs, ordered=True)
    model.delivery_cost = pyo.Param(
        model.arcs, initialize=costs, within=pyo.Reals
    )
    model.route = pyo.Var(model.arcs, domain=pyo.Binary)

    def outgoing_rule(instance, origin):
        return sum(
            instance.route[origin, destination]
            for destination in instance.cities
            if destination != origin
        ) == 1

    def incoming_rule(instance, destination):
        return sum(
            instance.route[origin, destination]
            for origin in instance.cities
            if origin != destination
        ) == 1

    model.outgoing_once = pyo.Constraint(
        model.cities, rule=outgoing_rule
    )
    model.incoming_once = pyo.Constraint(
        model.cities, rule=incoming_rule
    )

    model.subtour_limits = pyo.ConstraintList()
    for subset_size in range(2, len(cities)):
        for subset in combinations(cities, subset_size):
            model.subtour_limits.add(
                sum(
                    model.route[origin, destination]
                    for origin in subset
                    for destination in subset
                    if origin != destination
                )
                <= len(subset) - 1
            )

    model.total_cost = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(
            model.delivery_cost[origin, destination]
            * model.route[origin, destination]
            for origin, destination in model.arcs
        ),
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    try:
        Highs().solve(model)
    except RuntimeError as exc:
        if "a feasible solution was not found" in str(exc).lower():
            return {"objective": None, "status": "no_feasible_solution"}
        raise

    try:
        obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.total_cost))
    except ValueError:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "objective_unavailable"}

    return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
```

```python
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

def solve(params):
    cities = ["Alpha", "Bravo", "Charlie", "Delta"]
    n = len(cities)

    cost = {}
    for i in cities:
        for j in cities:
            if i != j:
                cost[(i, j)] = params["cost_{}_{}".format(i, j)]

    model = gp.Model("tsp")
    model.Params.OutputFlag = 0

    x = {}
    for i in cities:
        for j in cities:
            if i != j:
                x[(i, j)] = model.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="x_%s_%s" % (i, j))

    u = {}
    for i in cities:
        u[i] = model.addVar(lb=0, ub=n - 1, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="u_%s" % i)

    model.setObjective(
        gp.quicksum(cost[(i, j)] * x[(i, j)] for (i, j) in x), GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    for j in cities:
        model.addConstr(
            gp.quicksum(x[(i, j)] for i in cities if i != j) == 1,
            name="in_%s" % j,
        )
    for i in cities:
        model.addConstr(
            gp.quicksum(x[(i, j)] for j in cities if j != i) == 1,
            name="out_%s" % i,
        )

    # MTZ subtour elimination
    for i in cities:
        for j in cities:
            if i != j and i != cities[0] and j != cities[0]:
                model.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + n * x[(i, j)] <= n - 1,
                    name="mtz_%s_%s" % (i, j),
                )

    model.optimize()

    if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
        return {"objective": float(model.ObjVal), "status": "optimal"}
    elif model.Status == GRB.INFEASIBLE:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "infeasible"}
    else:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "failed"}
```

```
Imagine a logistics manager tasked with planning a route for a courier who needs to deliver packages to six different cities. The cities are labeled from 1 to 6. The courier has to start from any one of these cities, visit each of the other cities exactly once, and then return to the starting city. The main objective for the logistics manager is to design the route in such a way that the total travel cost is minimized.

Here is a breakdown of the travel costs between each pair of cities:
- The cost to travel from City 1 to City 2 is 23 units, to City 3 is 50 units, to City 4 is 92 units, to City 5 is 56 units, and to City 6 is 91 units.
- From City 2, the cost is 23 units to City 1, 38 units to City 3, 25 units to City 4, 25 units to City 5, and 69 units to City 6.
- From City 3, the travel costs are 50 units to City 1, 38 units to City 2, 66 units to City 4, 51 units to City 5, and 76 units to City 6.
- Traveling from City 4, it costs 92 units to City 1, 25 units to City 2, 66 units to City 3, 97 units to City 5, and 37 units to City 6.
- From City 5, the costs are 56 units to City 1, 25 units to City 2, 51 units to City 3, 97 units to City 4, and 30 units to City 6.
- Lastly, from City 6, it costs 91 units to go to City 1, 69 units to City 2, 76 units to City 3, 37 units to City 4, and 30 units to City 5.

What is the minimum total travel cost for the courier to visit each city exactly once and return to the starting city?
```

```python
import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.appsi.solvers.highs import Highs


def solve(params):
    num_cities = int(params["num_cities"])
    cost_matrix = params["cost_matrix"]

    cities = list(range(num_cities))

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    model.cities = pyo.Set(initialize=cities)

    # x[i, j] = 1 if arc i->j is used
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.cities, model.cities, domain=pyo.Binary)

    def arc_cost_rule(m):
        return sum(
            cost_matrix[i][j] * m.x[i, j]
            for i in cities
            for j in cities
            if i != j
        )

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=arc_cost_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Each city has exactly one outgoing arc
    def out_rule(m, i):
        return sum(m.x[i, j] for j in cities if j != i) == 1

    model.out_deg = pyo.Constraint(model.cities, rule=out_rule)

    # Each city has exactly one incoming arc
    def in_rule(m, j):
        return sum(m.x[i, j] for i in cities if i != j) == 1

    model.in_deg = pyo.Constraint(model.cities, rule=in_rule)

    # Fix diagonals to zero
    def diag_rule(m, i):
        return m.x[i, i] == 0

    model.no_self = pyo.Constraint(model.cities, rule=diag_rule)

    # Subtour elimination via ladder/MTZ-style ordering with continuous u
    # u[i] represents the position/order of city i in the tour (for i != root)
    root = cities[0]
    non_root = cities[1:]

    model.u = pyo.Var(non_root, bounds=(1, num_cities - 1))

    def mtz_rule(m, i, j):
        if i != j and j != root and i != root:
            return m.u[j] - m.u[i] >= 1 - (num_cities - 1) * (1 - m.x[i, j])
        return pyo.Constraint.Skip

    model.mtz = pyo.Constraint(
        [(i, j) for i in cities for j in cities if i != j], rule=mtz_rule
    )

    Highs().solve(model)

    obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.obj))
    return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
```

```python
        (i, j)
        for i in cities

        if i != j

    model.arcs = pyo.Set(dimen=2, initialize=arcs, ordered=True)
    model.travel_cost = pyo.Param(
        model.arcs,
        initialize={(i, j): cost_matrix[i][j] for i, j in arcs},
        within=pyo.Reals,
    )
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.arcs, domain=pyo.Binary)

    def outgoing_rule(instance, i):
        return sum(
            instance.x[i, j] for j in cities if j != i
        ) == 1

    def incoming_rule(instance, j):
        return sum(
            instance.x[i, j] for i in cities if i != j
        ) == 1

    model.outgoing = pyo.Constraint(model.cities, rule=outgoing_rule)
    model.incoming = pyo.Constraint(model.cities, rule=incoming_rule)

    model.subtour_elimination = pyo.ConstraintList()
    for subset_size in range(2, num_cities):
        for subset in combinations(cities, subset_size):
            model.subtour_elimination.add(
                sum(
                    model.x[i, j]
                    for i in subset
                    for j in subset
                    if i != j
                )
                <= subset_size - 1
            )

    model.total_cost = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(
            model.travel_cost[i, j] * model.x[i, j]
            for i, j in arcs
        ),
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    # Appsi raises RuntimeError when it cannot load a feasible solution.
    try:
        Highs().solve(model)
    except RuntimeError:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "solve_failed"}

    try:
        obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.total_cost))
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        return {"objective": None, "status": "objective_unavailable"}

    return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
```

```python
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

def solve(params):
    cost_matrix = params["cost_matrix"]
    num_cities = params["num_cities"]

    n = num_cities
    cities = list(range(n))

    model = gp.Model("TSP")
    model.setParam("OutputFlag", 0)

    # x[i,j] = 1 if courier travels from city i to city j
    x = {}
    for i in cities:
        for j in cities:
            if i != j:
                x[i, j] = model.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"x_{i}_{j}")

    # u[i] = position of city i in the tour (MTZ formulation), for i != 0
    u = {}
    for i in cities:
        if i != 0:
            u[i] = model.addVar(lb=1, ub=n - 1, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"u_{i}")

    # Objective: minimize total travel cost
    model.setObjective(
        gp.quicksum(cost_matrix[i][j] * x[i, j] for i in cities for j in cities if i != j),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # Each city is departed exactly once
    for i in cities:
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for j in cities if j != i) == 1, name=f"depart_{i}")

    # Each city is arrived at exactly once
    for j in cities:
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for i in cities if i != j) == 1, name=f"arrive_{j}")

    # MTZ subtour elimination constraints
    for i in cities:
        if i == 0:
            continue
        for j in cities:
            if j == 0 or i == j:
                continue
            model.addConstr(
                u[i] - u[j] + (n - 1) * x[i, j] <= n - 2,
                name=f"mtz_{i}_{j}"
            )

    model.optimize()

    if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
        return {"objective": model.ObjVal, "status": "optimal"}
    elif model.Status == GRB.INFEASIBLE:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "infeasible"}
    elif model.Status == GRB.UNBOUNDED:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "unbounded"}
    else:
        return {"objective": None, "status": f"status_{model.Status}"}
```

```python
import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.appsi.solvers.highs import Highs


def solve(params):
    num_cities = int(params["num_cities"])
    cities = list(range(1, num_cities + 1))

    cost = {}
    for i in cities:
        for j in cities:
            if i != j:
                cost[(i, j)] = params["cost_%d_%d" % (i, j)]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    model.CITY = pyo.Set(initialize=cities)
    model.ARC = pyo.Set(initialize=list(cost.keys()), dimen=2)

    model.x = pyo.Var(model.ARC, domain=pyo.Binary)
    model.u = pyo.Var(model.CITY, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(cost[(i, j)] * m.x[(i, j)] for (i, j) in m.ARC)
    model.total_cost = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    def out_rule(m, i):
        return sum(m.x[(i, j)] for j in m.CITY if i != j) == 1
    model.out_deg = pyo.Constraint(model.CITY, rule=out_rule)

    def in_rule(m, j):
        return sum(m.x[(i, j)] for i in m.CITY if i != j) == 1
    model.in_deg = pyo.Constraint(model.CITY, rule=in_rule)

    # MTZ subtour elimination
    def mtz_rule(m, i, j):
        if i != j and i >= 2 and j >= 2:
            return m.u[i] - m.u[j] + num_cities * m.x[(i, j)] <= num_cities - 1
        return pyo.Constraint.Skip
    model.mtz = pyo.Constraint(model.CITY, model.CITY, rule=mtz_rule)

    def lb_rule(m, i):
        if i >= 2:
            return m.u[i] >= 1
        return pyo.Constraint.Skip
    model.u_lb = pyo.Constraint(model.CITY, rule=lb_rule)

    def ub_rule(m, i):
        if i >= 2:
            return m.u[i] <= num_cities - 1
        return pyo.Constraint.Skip
    model.u_ub = pyo.Constraint(model.CITY, rule=ub_rule)

    Highs().solve(model)

    obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.total_cost))
    return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
```

```python
# IR: {"sets":{"V":"{1,...,num_cities} (frozen at six cities)","A":"{(i,j) in V x V: i != j}","U":"V \\ {1}"},"params":{"num_cities":"params['num_cities']","c[i,j]":"params['cost_i_j'] for (i,j) in A"},"variables":{"x[i,j]":"binary for (i,j) in A","u[i]":"continuous in [1,num_cities-1] for i in U"},"constraints":["sum(x[i,j] for j in V if j!=i)=1 for i in V","sum(x[i,j] for i in V if i!=j)=1 for j in V","u[i]-u[j]+num_cities*x[i,j]<=num_cities-1 for distinct i,j in U"],"objective":"minimize sum(c[i,j]*x[i,j] for (i,j) in A)"}

import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.appsi.solvers.highs import Highs


def solve(params):
    num_cities = params["num_cities"]
    if num_cities != 6:
        raise ValueError("num_cities must equal the frozen index-set size of six.")

    cities = tuple(range(1, num_cities + 1))
    arcs = tuple(
        (origin, destination)
        for origin in cities
        for destination in cities
        if origin != destination
    )
    other_cities = tuple(city for city in cities if city != 1)

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    model.cities = pyo.Set(initialize=cities, ordered=True)
    model.arcs = pyo.Set(dimen=2, initialize=arcs, ordered=True)
    model.other_cities = pyo.Set(initialize=other_cities, ordered=True)

    model.travel_cost = pyo.Param(
        model.arcs,
        initialize={
            (origin, destination): params[f"cost_{origin}_{destination}"]
            for origin, destination in arcs
        },
        within=pyo.Reals,
    )

    model.x = pyo.Var(model.arcs, domain=pyo.Binary)
    model.u = pyo.Var(
        model.other_cities,
        domain=pyo.Reals,
        bounds=(1, num_cities - 1),
    )

    def outgoing_rule(instance, origin):
        return sum(
            instance.x[origin, destination]
            for destination in instance.cities
            if destination != origin
        ) == 1

    def incoming_rule(instance, destination):
        return sum(
            instance.x[origin, destination]
            for origin in instance.cities
            if origin != destination
        ) == 1

    def subtour_rule(instance, origin, destination):
        if origin == destination:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        return (
            instance.u[origin]
            - instance.u[destination]
            + num_cities * instance.x[origin, destination]
            <= num_cities - 1
        )

    model.outgoing = pyo.Constraint(model.cities, rule=outgoing_rule)
    model.incoming = pyo.Constraint(model.cities, rule=incoming_rule)
    model.subtour_elimination = pyo.Constraint(
        model.other_cities,
        model.other_cities,
        rule=subtour_rule,
    )

    model.total_cost = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(
            model.travel_cost[origin, destination]
            * model.x[origin, destination]
            for origin, destination in model.arcs
        ),
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    try:
        Highs().solve(model)
    except RuntimeError as exc:
        if "a feasible solution was not found" not in str(exc).lower():
            raise
        # The solver could not load a feasible solution. Check the objective
        # below; objective retrievability is the sole success criterion.

    try:
        obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.total_cost))
    except ValueError:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "objective_unavailable"}

    return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
```

```python
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB
from itertools import combinations

def solve(params):
    n = int(params["num_cities"])
    cities = list(range(1, n + 1))

    # Build cost matrix from params
    cost = {}
    for i in cities:
        for j in cities:
            if i != j:
                cost[i, j] = params[f"cost_{i}_{j}"]

    model = gp.Model("TSP")
    model.setParam("OutputFlag", 0)

    # Binary decision variables: x[i,j] = 1 if travel from i to j
    x = model.addVars(cities, cities, vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="x")

    # No self-loops
    for i in cities:
        model.addConstr(x[i, i] == 0)

    # Objective: minimize total travel cost
    model.setObjective(
        gp.quicksum(cost[i, j] * x[i, j] for i in cities for j in cities if i != j),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # Each city is departed exactly once
    for i in cities:
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for j in cities if j != i) == 1)

    # Each city is entered exactly once
    for j in cities:
        model.addConstr(gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for i in cities if i != j) == 1)

    # MTZ subtour elimination
    # u[i] is the position of city i in the tour (continuous)
    u = model.addVars(cities, lb=1, ub=n, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="u")

    # Fix the starting city position to break symmetry
    model.addConstr(u[cities[0]] == 1)

    for i in cities:
        for j in cities[1:]:  # j != first city
            if i != j:
                model.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + n * x[i, j] <= n - 1
                )

    model.optimize()

    if model.Status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
        return {"objective": model.ObjVal, "status": "optimal"}
    elif model.Status == GRB.INFEASIBLE:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "infeasible"}
    elif model.Status == GRB.UNBOUNDED:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "unbounded"}
    else:
        return {"objective": None, "status": f"status_{model.Status}"}
```

### 2. Problem text

```
Imagine a delivery driver who needs to deliver packages to five different cities. These cities are represented as City 1, City 2, City 3, City 4, and City 5. The driver can start their route from any city, but they must deliver a package to each city exactly once before returning to the starting city. The objective is to find the route that minimizes the total travel cost. The cost could be based on factors such as distance, fuel consumption, or time spent.

Here are the details of the travel costs between the cities:

The cost to travel from City 1 to City 2 is 82 units, to City 3 is 76 units, to City 4 is 92 units, and to City 5 is 59 units.
From City 2, it costs 82 units to return to City 1, 98 units to travel to City 3, 58 units to City 4, and 82 units to City 5.
When leaving from City 3, it costs 76 units to reach City 1, 98 units to get to City 2, 26 units to travel to City 4 and 74 units to travel to City 5.
From City 4, the costs are 92 units to City 1, 58 units to City 2, 26 units to City 3 and 96 units to City 5.
Lastly, from City 5, it costs 59 units to go to City 1, 82 units to travel to City 2, 74 units to City 3, and 96 units to reach City 4.

Given these costs, what is the minimum total cost for the delivery driver to deliver packages to each city exactly once and return to the starting city?
```

```python
import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.appsi.solvers.highs import Highs


def solve(params):
    cost_matrix = params["cost_matrix"]
    n = len(cost_matrix)
    cities = list(range(n))

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Binary arc variables: x[i,j] = 1 if the route goes from city i directly to city j
    model.x = pyo.Var(cities, cities, domain=pyo.Binary)

    # Objective: minimize total travel cost
    model.total_cost = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(cost_matrix[i][j] * model.x[i, j]
                 for i in cities for j in cities if i != j),
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    # Each city is departed exactly once
    model.depart = pyo.ConstraintList()
    for i in cities:
        model.depart.add(
            sum(model.x[i, j] for j in cities if j != i) == 1
        )

    # Each city is entered exactly once
    model.arrive = pyo.ConstraintList()
    for j in cities:
        model.arrive.add(
            sum(model.x[i, j] for i in cities if i != j) == 1
        )

    # Subtour elimination (order/MTZ formulation)
    # u[i] is the position of city i in the tour (used for all but a reference city)
    model.u = pyo.Var(cities, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, n - 1))
    # Fix reference city 0 position to 0 (removes symmetry)
    model.u[0].fix(0)

    model.subtour = pyo.ConstraintList()
    for i in cities:
        for j in cities:
            if i != j and i != 0 and j != 0:
                model.subtour.add(
                    model.u[i] - model.u[j] + (n - 1) * model.x[i, j] <= n - 2
                )

    solver = Highs()
    solver.solve(model)

    obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.total_cost))
    return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
```

```python
from itertools import combinations

import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.appsi.solvers.highs import Highs


def solve(params):
    cost_matrix = params["cost_matrix"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.cities = pyo.RangeSet(0, 4)
    model.arcs = pyo.Set(
        dimen=2,
        initialize=[
            (i, j)
            for i in model.cities
            for j in model.cities
            if i != j
        ],
    )

    model.travel_cost = pyo.Param(
        model.arcs,
        initialize={
            (i, j): cost_matrix[i][j]
            for i, j in model.arcs
        },
        within=pyo.Reals,
    )

    model.x = pyo.Var(model.arcs, domain=pyo.Binary)

    def outgoing_rule(instance, i):
        return sum(
            instance.x[i, j] for j in instance.cities if j != i
        ) == 1

    def incoming_rule(instance, j):
        return sum(
            instance.x[i, j] for i in instance.cities if i != j
        ) == 1

    model.outgoing_constraints = pyo.Constraint(
        model.cities, rule=outgoing_rule
    )
    model.incoming_constraints = pyo.Constraint(
        model.cities, rule=incoming_rule
    )

    model.subtour_constraints = pyo.ConstraintList()
    cities = tuple(model.cities)
    for subset_size in range(2, len(cities)):
        for subset in combinations(cities, subset_size):
            model.subtour_constraints.add(
                sum(
                    model.x[i, j]
                    for i in subset
                    for j in subset
                    if i != j
                )
                <= len(subset) - 1
            )

    model.total_cost = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(
            model.travel_cost[i, j] * model.x[i, j]
            for i, j in model.arcs
        ),
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    try:
        Highs().solve(model)
    except RuntimeError:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "solve_failed"}

    try:
        obj_val = float(pyo.value(model.total_cost))
    except ValueError:
        return {"objective": None, "status": "objective_unavailable"}

    return {"objective": obj_val, "status": "optimal"}
```
